VERDICT: CONFIRM C0039 — Evidence: `_create_sandbox()` computes `common = os.path.commonpath(all_paths)` from the exact source files plus target. When reviewing a single file set from one directory, `common` can collapse to a leaf directory instead of a stable project root, so copied files lose their original package anchoring. The function comment promises preserved package structure for import resolution; this base selection breaks that promise.

VERDICT: CONFIRM C0040 — Evidence: `_apply_fix_to_source()` compiles `line_pattern = re.compile(r"[Ll]ines?\s+(\d+)(?:\s*[-–]\s*(\d+))?:\s*(.+?)\s*->\s*(.+)")` without `re.DOTALL`. For common multi-line fix text like `Lines 10-12: old_block -> new_block`, `old_block`/`new_block` cannot span embedded newlines, so multi-line line-range replacements never match.

VERDICT: CONFIRM C0041 — Evidence: `compute_pacing_signals()` emits the response-size anomaly in check 4 with `signal_type="context_growth"`. That conflates two distinct signal sources, so downstream consumers cannot distinguish cumulative context budget pressure from one model producing anomalously large output.

VERDICT: CONFIRM C0038 — Evidence: `_categorise_ruff()` immediately maps every `F*` code to `DEAD_CODE`. Ruff/Pyflakes F-codes include correctness errors like `F821 undefined name`, `F823 local variable referenced before assignment`, `F722 syntax error in forward annotation`, not just unused imports/dead code. This silently misclassifies real bugs as dead code.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` silently drops all diagnostics when pyright exits non-zero with valid JSON only on `stdout` absent or malformed, because parse failure is only logged and returns `[]` (`except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError): logger.warning(...)`). Pyright commonly returns structured failure information via non-success exit or stderr on config/environment errors. In this module, that becomes indistinguishable from “no issues found,” causing the health scan to report a clean state even when the tool failed to analyze.
FOLLOW: `scan_health()` treats any normal return from `run_pyright()` as `tools_available["pyright"] = True` and aggregates zero diagnostics. That feeds incorrect health signals to the insect brain, masks analyzer failure in the report, and corrupts fix evaluation because `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, ...)` also interprets the same failure mode as zero new type errors. A broken pyright invocation can therefore produce both false-clean health scans and false SAFE/NEUTRAL fix verdicts.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — In `run_pyright()`, treat non-JSON output or `returncode == -1`/timeout as tool failure, not empty diagnostics: raise `ToolNotFoundError` for missing binary and raise a normal exception (or dedicated parse/tool-failure exception) when output cannot be parsed or the process times out, so callers mark the tool unavailable/failed instead of “0 findings.”
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.90
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` runs tests in the sandbox with `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)` but does not rewrite the executable path itself. The immune pipeline passes `test_cmd=["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]` from context. In a multi-interpreter setup, this invokes whatever `python3` is on PATH, not the same 3.13 toolchain hardcoded for pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy, and not necessarily the interpreter expected by the copied sandbox environment. This creates an interface mismatch between endocrine fix evaluation and immune pipeline assumptions.
FOLLOW: Even if test path rewriting bugs are fixed elsewhere, tests can still run under a different interpreter than the static analyzers and source environment. A fix may appear SAFE because tests pass under the wrong interpreter, or HARMFUL because pytest/imports fail under an unintended interpreter, producing misleading verification signals that the immune pipeline uses to set `verified=True`.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Before running `test_cmd`, rewrite a leading bare `"python"`/`"python3"` executable to `PYTHON_313` so the test subprocess uses the same interpreter family as the rest of the endocrine toolchain.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` marks a fix SAFE whenever `tests_passed is True`, even if no diagnostic counts improved and even if the target bug was not actually affected. The code path is: after rejecting positive net deltas, it computes `total_net`; if `total_net < 0` return SAFE; then `if result.tests_passed is True: return "SAFE"`; else NEUTRAL. That means “tests happened to pass” upgrades a no-op patch to SAFE.
FOLLOW: In the immune pipeline, `run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` for `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL`, but the SAFE label still matters as the endocrine layer’s direct output and may be consumed by humans or future logic as stronger evidence than NEUTRAL. Mislabeling no-op or irrelevant fixes as SAFE degrades trust in fix evaluation and can prematurely close bugs if consumers later distinguish SAFE from NEUTRAL.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — In `_compute_fix_verdict()`, only return SAFE when tests pass and at least one issue count improves (`total_net < 0`); if tests pass with `total_net == 0`, return NEUTRAL.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` novelty plateau threshold and emitted metric are internally inconsistent. The condition is `all(n <= 1 for n in recent)`, but the emitted signal uses `threshold=float(window)` where `window = 3`. The actual decision boundary is “every round in the last 3 had novelty <=1”; the recorded threshold says “3”. This metadata does not describe the trigger that fired.
FOLLOW: The insect brain receives pacing signals as structured control data. If a novelty plateau signal says `metric_value=2.0 threshold=3.0`, downstream logging or dashboards imply a sum-based comparison, but the actual predicate was per-round. This can mislead human review and any downstream logic that inspects `metric_value`/`threshold` rather than recomputing from `detail`.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Set the novelty plateau signal metadata to match the real predicate, e.g. `metric_value=float(max(recent))` and `threshold=1.0`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.68
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — The advertised “defect detection” capability is still incomplete at the coordinator level even beyond the already-registered missing public API. `scan_health()` only aggregates raw category counts from tool diagnostics; it never produces the documented defect categories “off-by-one, race conditions, security, dead code” as a distinct stage output or report field separate from tool output. `EndocrineReport` has `health_scan`, `fix_evaluations`, and `pacing_signals`, but no defect-detection result object.
FOLLOW: The module claims four endocrine functions, but consumers only receive tool diagnostics plus counts. Even if a helper API is later added, the coordinator currently does not expose defect detection as part of the inter-round report handed to the insect brain. This leaves one documented feature effectively non-firing in the real integration path.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Add a `defect_summary` field to `EndocrineReport` and populate it in `EndocrineLayer.run()` using the existing diagnostic categories/counts, without extra inference complexity.
VERIFIED: TRUE
